subject: NimbusCare: production latency & 5xx spike — routing suspicion
messages:
From: Alex Carter <alex.carter@nimbuscare.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Cc: SaaS Ops <ops@nimbuscare.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 08:05:00 -0700
Subject: High latency & 5xx spike in prod (US-West) — immediate assistance needed

Lauren,

We started seeing a sharp increase in 50x errors and tail latency for our inference calls around 07:40 PST. Error rate jumped from ~0.3% to 6% and P99 moved from 120ms to 1.6s. This is impacting checkout flows in a few critical clinics.

What we observed: 
- Errors are primarily 502/504 and occasional connection resets.
- Most failures map to calls routed via us-west-2 endpoints.
- DNS lookups for model-endpoint.redwood.com occasionally time out (100s of ms) before succeeding.

We collected packet traces and a short error log attached (error-sample.log). Can you confirm whether there's an existing incident on your side or any recent peering/firewall changes? We need an ETA for a mitigation and whether you can initiate a failover to a backup path while you investigate root cause.

Alex Carter
Head of Platform, NimbusCare
alex.carter@nimbuscare.com
[attachment: error-sample.log (text)]

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
To: Alex Carter <alex.carter@nimbuscare.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: High latency & 5xx spike in prod (US-West) — immediate assistance needed

Alex — thanks for the quick flag. I'm escalating to the SRE and engagement teams, looping in Marissa for immediate triage and Vivek for executive visibility.

Immediate actions we are initiating:
1) SRE will start a live trace and look at our peering/egress metrics for us-west-2.
2) We will attempt a controlled region failover for a subset of traffic (canary) to us-east-1 to see if error rate normalizes.
3) If DNS timeouts continue, we'll provision a temporary fixed-resolver route for your account and push a bypass for the affected prefixes.

Please confirm the most critical customer flows (API keys / routes) you want prioritized for the canary. Also, can you share the last 60s of your client-side timestamps for failed requests (if possible)?

I'll keep this thread as the single source of updates.

— Lauren
VP Sales, Redwood Inference
lauren@redwood.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>, Alex Carter <alex.carter@nimbuscare.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 09:11:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: High latency & 5xx spike in prod (US-West) — immediate assistance needed

Alex / team — quick technical update from triage: 

What we found so far (10:00 PST):
- At ~07:36 PST we see a burst of SYN retransmits from our egress nodes to a subset of NimbusCare IPs; packet-level traces indicate intermittent packet loss between our peering fabric and the upstream transit provider. Attached is a short pcap (trace-1123.pcap) with one example flow.
- Concurrently our resolver logs show a spike in NXDOMAIN / timeout responses for the model endpoint; timeouts line up with the observed 502/504 windows.
- Firewall appliance in front of the affected transit path shows a sudden increase in queued sessions (~3x baseline) before we started seeing resets.

Short-term mitigation we applied (08:58 PST):
- Partial traffic re-route: we diverted ~25% of your traffic to our us-east-1 pool (canary) — error rate for that canary dropped to ~0.6% within 3 minutes.
- Increased TCP retries and extended idle timeouts on the affected proxy to prevent premature resets.

Next steps (we are executing now):
- Opened an incident with the transit provider to confirm peering health and BGP flap history.
- Rolling a temporary DNS resolver override for your account to eliminate intermittent resolver failures (will take effect in ~7 minutes).
- Preparing a configuration to pin critical routes to the alternate path if the canary remains healthy.

Attachments: trace-1123.pcap (pcap) — included for your network team.

I will post a follow-up with the transit provider response and a recommended permanent remediation (likely a peering prioritization or additional egress pair).

— Marissa
Customer Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
[attachment: trace-1123.pcap (pcap)]

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Alex Carter <alex.carter@nimbuscare.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 12:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: High latency & 5xx spike in prod (US-West) — immediate assistance needed

Team — thanks for the rapid triage. Two asks for alignment with NimbusCare execs: 

1) Can someone produce a two-slide exec brief (cause, impact, mitigation, next steps + ETA) I can share with our CRO and NimbusCare leadership by 13:30 PST?
2) Alex — we need a short note from you quantifying business impact (approx. number of affected requests/min and whether this puts any clinics into degraded mode). We will also prep a goodwill credit proposal; Rishi can align commercial terms.

Marissa — please include an initial RCA hypothesis in the brief (peering degradation + resolver timeouts) and convert the temporary bypass to a documented plan we can ship ASAP.

Vivek
CTO, Redwood Inference

From: Alex Carter <alex.carter@nimbuscare.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Cc: SaaS Ops <ops@nimbuscare.com>, Nina Park <nina.park@nimbuscare.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 15:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: High latency & 5xx spike in prod (US-West) — immediate assistance needed

Thanks — the canary helped and error rates are back down to ~0.9% overall, latency P99 is back under 300ms for the canary hosts. A few items: 

- We still see intermittent 502s (~0.9% concentrated to a specific AZ) which suggests the root cause is not fully resolved.
- For the exec brief: I can provide impact numbers — during the 07:36–08:10 window we saw ~1,700 failed inference calls (rough estimate) across 14 clinics; a handful reported degraded checkout flows but no data loss.
- We will accept an interim goodwill credit; Rishi — please send the standard incident credit proposal and any next-step compensation language for our procurement team.

I've attached a short error snippet for your SREs (error-sample.log) and a PDF describing our SLA impact request (nimbuscare_sla_request.pdf). Please keep us posted on the permanent remediation ETA.

Alex
Head of Platform, NimbusCare
